area_overview: Parsing and formatting DateTime/DateTimeOffset values safely: flexible parse, exact parse, standard format specifiers, custom format tokens, ISO 8601, RFC 1123, and Unix time.
key_ideas: Parse/TryParse are flexible and culture-sensitive; TryParse is safer for invalid input.
ParseExact/TryParseExact should be used when the input must match a known format.
DateTimeOffset.Parse is better when the input can contain an offset and that offset should be preserved.
Standard formats like O/o, s, u, and R have specific API/log/header uses.
Plain ToString() without a format is culture-dependent and should not be used for APIs, persistence, logs, or sorting.
Custom format tokens are case-sensitive: M vs m, H vs h, f vs F matter.
ISO 8601 is the default for JSON/public API textual timestamps; RFC 1123 is for HTTP headers; Unix time is for compact numeric timestamps.
